summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived article on Queen Elizabeth II, covering her early life and line of succession, her wartime service and education, her 1947 marriage to Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, her accession in February 1952, and her long reign over the United Kingdom and Commonwealth realms. It also covers her record-setting longevity, her role in the Commonwealth's transformation, her children and grandchildren, and her private and trust-held property. The note repeats some passages, and it contains navigation-style realm lists that are reproduced without added analysis.
one_line: Biography of Queen Elizabeth II, covering her early life, succession, wartime service, reign from 1952, records and family.
key_facts: Elizabeth was born 21 April 1926 and has been Queen of the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand since 6 February 1952.
Her first child, Prince Charles, was born on 14 November 1948, and Princess Anne was born in 1950.
When her grandfather died in 1936 and Edward succeeded as Edward VIII, Elizabeth became second-in-line to the throne, after her father.
Edward VIII abdicated later in 1936 after his proposed marriage to divorced socialite Wallis Simpson provoked a constitutional crisis.
In 1947, Elizabeth married Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, with whom she has four children: Charles, Anne, Andrew, and Edward.
The Queen opened the 1976 Summer Olympics in Montreal and the 2012 Summer Olympics and Paralympics in London, making her the first head of state to open two Olympic Games in two different countries.
On 4 April 2013, she received an honorary BAFTA for her patronage of the film industry and was called "the most memorable Bond girl yet" at the award ceremony.
Elizabeth surpassed Queen Victoria to become the longest-lived British monarch in December 2007, and the longest-reigning British monarch on 9 September 2015.
She is the longest-reigning queen regnant in history, the world's oldest reigning monarch, and second-longest-serving current head of state after King Bhumibol Adulyadej of Thailand.
In 1953, the Queen and her husband embarked on a seven-month round-the-world tour, visiting 13 countries and covering more than 40,000 miles.
In 1940, the 14-year-old Elizabeth made her first radio broadcast during the BBC's Children's Hour, addressing other children who had been evacuated from the cities.
When George VI's death occurred on 6 February 1952 while Elizabeth was in Kenya, Philip broke the news to the new Queen, and she chose to remain Elizabeth as her regnal name.
In 2017, she became the first British monarch to reach a Sapphire Jubilee.

The Royal Collection and the British Crown Estate are held in trust by the sovereign and cannot be sold or owned by Elizabeth in a private capacity, while Sandringham House and Balmoral Castle are privately owned by her.
In 1946, she was inducted into the Welsh Gorsedd of Bards at the National Eisteddfod of Wales.
